decisions.reason: As a height-adjustable executive desk system it sits squarely in the firm's core office offer and future focus on flexible workplaces, so sunk development effort and visible market commitment make management likely to continue it.

The chair family is close to the established portfolio and likely required meaningful design and variant investment, which under escalation of commitment favors retaining it unless failure is unmistakable.

Floor cushions from carpets are a more niche extension with lower strategic centrality than the firm's main furniture lines, so despite some public commitment management has less reason to defend it further.
The soft upholstered sofa received especially visible promotion and designer-linked launch messaging, making withdrawal more costly reputationally and therefore less likely.
A high standing table fits the firm's workplace and conference direction and likely shares development and sales logic with existing products, so management is inclined to keep it on the market.
The rug collection is the most distant from the established offer, so it is easier to justify cutting it and reallocating resources once it no longer looks like a temporary experiment.
